prompt:
Style: fresh-illustration. Transform the supplied ORIGINAL photograph of a LEGO Millennium Falcon model on a white cabinet, minifigures, a display plaque and nearby autumn foliage. Render only a single full-frame artwork using this style treatment:

The surroundings may be extended to fill 3:4 but never stretched, distorted, repainted or rearranged. - **artwork — selection.** Do not redraw the whole scene. First find the photo's 3 visual memory points: (1) the main subject, (2) its key action / pose / relationship, (3) the most recognizable environmental cue or silhouette. Only those are reinterpreted as a clean hand-drawn 2D cartoon illustration. - **artwork — reduction.** Remove 70–85% of secondary visual information; keep 50–75% of the half as negative space. The focus stays concentrated; the environment is not recreated. - **artwork — style.** Refined editorial cartoon — explicitly not a childish picture-book or toy-cute look. Clean black outlines with slight hand-drawn line-weight variation, flat soft pastel color fields, only minimal cel shading. Subjects may be simplified but keep their recognizable identity, pose and expression; textures are simplified into clean shapes. Fully 2D — no photorealism, no 3D, no collage. - **artwork — palette.** The photo's 2–5 most memorable key colors, reorganized into a soft, low-saturation pastel palette (light sky blue, soft green, warm skin tones, gentle pink, cream, off-white, pale beige, light yellow…). Bright, fresh and calm, never harsh; the negative space stays clean and airy. - **artwork — must preserve.** The main subject's identity, the number of people and their main interactions, the main pose/action, and the key building / object / landscape silhouette. Clothing, poses and faces must not be redesigned. The final check repeats the numbers: 50/50 halves, strict 3:4, 70–85% removed, 50–75% negative space, palette from the photo's own key colors. 

Preserve the original scene's subject relationships. Every part of the canvas must belong to the transformed artwork. No original photo panel, no before/after comparison, no split, no text.
